markscheme.html:
a.i

Use of Snell's law n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂ with n=c/v;
= c × sin(33°)/sin(45°);
≈ 0.77c OR 2.3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹;

Award [1] for setting up the correct relationship. Award [1] for the correct final answer. Using c = 3.00e8 m/s gives 2.31e8 m/s.

a.ii

The wavelength decreases;
Frequency remains constant at a boundary, and since speed decreases (v=fλ), the wavelength must decrease.

Award [1] for stating wavelength decreases. Award [1] for the explanation linking constant frequency and decreased speed.

a.iii

Angle of incidence at Q is θ_i = 90° - 33° = 57°;
Critical angle is given by sin(θ_c) = /c ≈ 0.77, so θ_c ≈ 50.4°;
Since θ_i (57°) > θ_c (50.4°), total internal reflection occurs and the light does not emerge at Q.

Award [1] for correct geometry to find the incidence angle at Q. Award [1] for calculating the critical angle. Award [1] for the comparison and correct conclusion.

b.i

Net force = Buoyant Force - Weight = (ρ_water - ρ_ice)Vg;
Newton's second law: = × a = (ρ_ice V)a;
a = g(ρ_water - ρ_ice)/ρ_ice = 9.81(1000 - 920)/920 ≈ 0.85 m s⁻² (upwards).

Award [1] for the net force expression. Award [1] for applying F=ma. Award [1] for the correct calculation. Accept g=10 m/s², giving a ≈ 0.87 m/s².

b.ii

The acceleration decreases with time (from its initial maximum value towards zero).

b.iii

Upward arrow labelled 'Buoyant force' or 'Upthrust'.
Two downward arrows labelled 'Weight' (or 'mg') and 'Drag'.
The length of the upward arrow must be equal to the sum of the lengths of the two downward arrows.

Award [1] for all three forces correctly identified and directed. Award [1] for showing the zero net force condition with vector lengths.

c.i

P = Fv => F = P/v = 3.1 / 0.50 = 6.2 N.

c.ii

At constant speed, friction force = F = 6.2 N. Normal force N = mg = 5.5 × 9.81 N.
μ_k = / N = 6.2 / (5.5 × 9.81) ≈ 0.11.

Calculation must show that friction equals the pulling force and normal force equals weight.

d.i

Work is done against the frictional force, generating thermal energy at the bottom surface of the ice, increasing its temperature;
The top surface is assumed to remain at the ambient temperature (-8.0 °C), so a temperature difference is created across the height of the block, resulting in a temperature gradient.

d.ii

Rate of heat flow P = 3.1 W. Using P = kA(ΔT/L);
ΔT = PL / (kA) = (3.1 × 8.0×10⁻²) / (2.3 × 7.5×10⁻²) ≈ 1.44 K;
= + ΔT = -8.0 + 1.44 ≈ -6.6 °C.

Award [1] for calculating ΔT. Award [1] for finding the final temperature. The rate of heat flow is the power dissipated by friction.

d.iii

Conduction from the bottom of the ice block into the table surface.

Other valid answers include: conduction from the sides of the ice to the surrounding air, or from the bottom surface of the ice to the air.

question.html:
8. A ray of light enters a rectangular block of ice from the air at point P, as shown. The angle of incidence at P is 45° and the angle of refraction is 33°. The refracted ray is incident on the adjacent ice-air boundary at point Q.

[Diagram: rectangular block labelled "block of ice" with air above. Incident ray in air strikes the top surface at P. Angle of incidence to the normal at P is 45°. Refracted ray inside the block makes an angle of 33° to the normal and travels down/right to point Q on the right side of the block.]

The speed of light in air is c.

a.i Calculate the speed of light in ice. [2]

a.ii State and explain the wavelength change entering ice. [2]

a.iii Deduce whether the light emerges at Q. [3]

b.i Determine the initial acceleration of a submerged ice block released from rest. [3]

b.ii State how acceleration changes with time when drag increases with speed and terminal speed is reached. [1]

b.iii Draw a free-body diagram at terminal speed. [2]

c.i Calculate the magnitude of the pulling force F from power and speed. [1]

c.ii Calculate the coefficient of dynamic friction. [1]

d.i Explain why there is a temperature gradient through the ice while it is pulled. [2]

d.ii Estimate the temperature of the bottom surface. [2]

d.iii Suggest another way energy is transferred through conduction in the system. [1]

issues.message: The normalized prompt omits the density data and drag setup for part b and the power, speed, mass, geometry, conductivity, and temperature data for parts c-d from source pages 20-25; the ray and force diagrams also remain descriptions rather than matched assets.
